function: no_learning, p. 2: MIMO-OFDM channel estimation by a model-based Quasi-NN whose weights are the path parameters, fitted to each pilot block by gradients and BFGS; nothing is trained.
notes: PDF checked: p. 1 holds the title and DOI 10.1109/TCOMM.2025.3594785. Exclusion no_learning, the first code that applies (it is a research article that proposes and evaluates a method). The Quasi-NN is the signal model (2) drawn as layers, and its weights are the gains, DoA, DoD and delays of the current channel (p. 3: "where the weights represent the key physical parameters to be optimized"). Its "online network training" (p. 1) fits them to the received pilots by minimizing the least-squares cost (5) with chain-rule gradients and BFGS (p. 3: "we then use the BFGS algorithm [36] to minimize the cost function"), so it is an iterative parametric estimator with no training data and no trained parameters; the paper sets it apart from deep unfolding, which relies on training data (p. 2: "In contrast, the Quasi-NN is fully model-based and functions as a white-box network"). The other components are classical too: initialization by 2D-IFFT peak detection (SDE, pp. 4-5), node merging and pruning by hypothesis tests with analytic F-distribution thresholds (pp. 5-6, 12-13), and in LA-QNN a location-parameter database filled with Quasi-NN estimates at reference points and read by nearest-point lookup (p. 7). For the reviewer: if the Quasi-NN were judged learned, the work would be area 2 (NMSE of the channel estimate, p. 9) on DeepMIMO 'O1' ray tracing (p. 9).
